script: Can you walk me through your typical lunch break routine when working from home or office, and how often do you order food in advance?
How do you currently handle situations where restaurants are out of stock on the dishes you're craving (e.g. jollof rice), and what alternatives have you tried?
Would you be willing to pay a premium for a convenient, hot meal delivered to your office within an hour of ordering, and if so, how much would that amount be?
interview_answers:
My typical lunch break routine is pretty straightforward. I work as a marketing coordinator, so my days are usually filled with meetings, emails, and social media tasks. When I'm at the office, I usually grab something quick from the cafeteria or bring my own lunch from home. But since I work from home sometimes, it can get a bit tricky.

If I do end up working from home, I'll often order food in advance because time is really limited for me. Usually, if I know what's going to happen that day, I'll place an order with a local WhatsApp vendor who delivers Nigerian home-style lunches – jollof rice, egusi soup, moi moi... those kinds of things are always a hit with my coworkers and me.

I'd say about 2-3 times a week, I'll order food in advance for the day. It's just so convenient because I know exactly what I want, and it saves me so much time. Plus, it's easier to eat while working, you know? Sometimes I feel like cooking at home is just too much work when I'm already stuck inside all day.

Honestly, it's not uncommon for me to get a message from my WhatsApp vendor saying that they're out of stock on some of the items I'm looking for. Usually, it's just a simple case of them running low on ingredients or having a busy day.

What I do in those situations is usually ask them if they have any alternatives or suggestions. Like, if they're out of jollof rice, maybe they can make me egusi soup instead? Or if they're out of moi moi, maybe they can add some fried plantains to the order?

Sometimes, my vendors will be able to hook me up with something similar, and it's actually not that bad. I mean, egusi soup is still a favorite of mine! But other times... well, let's just say I've learned to be patient and flexible when ordering food in advance.

I haven't really had to get creative or try new things too much, but if I'm being completely honest, sometimes I do end up getting something a bit different from what I originally ordered. And you know what? It's not always a disaster!

Honestly, I'm not sure about paying a premium for something. As it is, 2-3 times a week, I already spend around 5,000 - 7,000 Naira (depending on what I order) on food through WhatsApp vendors. That's a decent chunk of my budget.

To be honest, I'd need to know that the meal would really be worth an extra 1,000-2,000 Naira or more per order for me to consider it. It sounds like a lot, but if it means getting a hot meal in under an hour and saving time on cooking myself, I might be willing to pay a bit more.

But at the end of the day, my budget is pretty tight, and I'm not sure I'd be able to justify spending that much extra money on food.
